neighbours.label: 'you and your' on its way to a spouse, in a statement addressed to a married reader (usually about tax or accounts); a sentence without a marriage context stays quiet
fire: If you are married, you and your spouse can file a joint return.
Since you're married, both you and your wife can open an account.
Married couples: you and your husband may each give ten thousand dollars.
Once you marry, you and your partner share the tax bill.
As a married couple, both you and your spouse must sign the form.
If you're married and both you and your spouse work, you can claim it.
Married taxpayers can deduct what you and your spouse paid.
When you are married, both you and your husband are liable.
quiet: If you are single, you can file a simple return.
Since you're a student, you can open an account.
Retired people may each give ten thousand dollars.
Once you retire, you and your dog can share the house.
As a new customer, you must sign the form.
If you're young and you work, you can claim it.
Single taxpayers can deduct what they paid.
When you are renting, you and your friend are liable.

notes: Card: ' E' x4, ' your' x3, ' the' x3, ' and' x2, ' her' before spouse; the + pole's logit effect promotes ' partner', ' partners', so the - pole reads against that. Probe: 'married and both you and your' 0.62; 'Both you and your dog' 0.02, 'his or her spouse' 0.04, ' E' of E-mini 0.07. So this is one narrow slice and rests on one probe.
